# @game-studio/server-comms

Contains definitions for class to handle the Server comms for our games

ReqResServer is a Request-Response style connection to handle the Resume/Begin and Continue requests made by our Slot/Scratchcard games.

TODO: add info on Websocket server once implemented

## Usage

### ReqResServer
```ts
// if needed extend the Request and Response interfaces
interface IBeginEx extends IBeginRequest {
    newThing: string;
}
interface IResponseEx extends IGameServerResponse {
    anotherNewThing: string;
}

// instantiate the Server with your extended response type and any required urls
const server = new ReqResServer<ResponseEx>({ begin: '', resume: '' });
// hook up to any desired events e.g.
server.on('ON_SUCCESSFUL_RESPONSE', (response) => { console.log(response); });
server.on('ON_PROMO_RESULT', (promoDetails) => { promoDetails.forEach((promo) => { console.log(promo); }) });
server.on('ON_ERROR_TO_NOTIFY', (resultCodeData) => { console.log(resultCodeData); });
// for all events see src/request-response/events.ts

// Can then make resume/begin/continue requests like so
const beginBody: BeginEx = {
    ClientTypeId: 0,
    CrossCheck: 0,
    newThing: '',
    Skin: '',
    UserId: 0
};
server.begin(beginBody).then((result) => {
    result.anotherNewThing;
});
```

## Development

### Testing

```
npm run test
```
```
npm run test:continuous
```

Testing is ran using Karma and will execute all `**/*.spec.ts` files within the `tests` folder.

The `:continuous` flag is useful while developing because it will watch for changes in the source code and tests and execute the suite accordingly.

#### Coverage

Test coverage is generated and available under `reports/coverage` once a test run has completed.

### Linting

```
npm run lint
```

Runs `eslint` and outputs any errors.

### Building and Documentation

```
npm run build
```

This will clean the distribution folder, build the project and generate the documentation.

### Publishing

This package should not be published manually. Publishing is handled by the parent [game-studio](https://github.com/tombolaltd/game-studio) using lerna.

**Note:** it's worth noting that the private registry the package is published to is defined in the `package.json` file.

### TypeScript

#### tsconfig.json

This package is built in TypeScript and the options are controlled by `tsconfig.json` for use in the IDE.
